name: Containerlab
what_it_is: A CLI tool for orchestrating and managing container-based networking labs, automating container startup and virtual network wiring between nodes to form topologies defined in declarative YAML files. It supports 50+ NOS kinds spanning containerized and VM-backed platforms from Nokia, Arista, Cisco, Juniper, and others.
components: topology-engine: parses declarative .clab YAML files and translates them into running labs
kind-abstraction-layer: normalizes startup and configuration differences across NOS platforms
network-wiring-machinery: creates veth pairs and Linux bridge/OVS links between container interfaces
lab-lifecycle-manager: deploy, destroy, save, inspect, and graph operations
tls-provisioner: automated certificate generation for management plane access
clos-generator: built-in topology generator for scaled CLOS/fabric lab creation
vrnetlab-integration: wraps legacy VM-based routers in a thin Docker container for unified handling
measurement: No native traffic measurement engine; relies on external telemetry stacks connected to lab nodes
Integrates with test/traffic-generator nodes: Keysight IXIA-C, Spirent TestCenter, Ostinato
Node state inspection via 'containerlab inspect' (status, management IP, port mappings)
configuration: Declarative topology files (.clab.yml) define nodes, kinds, images, links, and management settings
Per-node startup-config injection supported for most NOS kinds
Automated TLS certificate provisioning for nodes that require it
Environment variables and bind-mount paths configurable per node in topology file
Labels and node groups supported for selective operations
fault_injection: No native fault-injection primitives; disruptions must be applied manually via Docker or Linux tc/iptables on the host
Link impairment (delay, loss, corruption) possible through Linux tc netem on veth interfaces outside containerlab
modes: interactive: CLI-driven lab deploy/destroy for development and demos
ci-cd: non-interactive mode suitable for pipeline integration
graph: generates topology diagrams from .clab files without deploying
save: snapshots running node configurations back to the filesystem
constraints: Requires Linux host with Docker; does not run natively on macOS or Windows without a Linux VM
VM-backed NOS images (vrnetlab) must be built separately by the user from vendor-supplied ISOs — images are not redistributed
Container-based NOS images (cEOS, XRd, cRPD) require vendor-specific licensing and image pull agreements
Concurrent topology deployments share the host kernel network namespace, so interface name collisions must be managed
No built-in traffic generation or packet capture; external tools (tcpdump, IXIA-C, Ostinato) must be added as lab nodes
notable_absences: No docker-compose file; Containerlab itself is the orchestration layer and runs as a single binary
No native fault injection or link impairment controls
No built-in telemetry collection or metrics storage; telemetry stack must be deployed separately
No GUI or web dashboard included in the core tool (graph command produces static diagrams only)
